questions.question: What is the valid range of index subscripts for an array of size N in C++?
questions.explanation: In C++, arrays are zero-bounded, meaning the first element is located at index 0 and the last element is at index N-1.

questions.question: Which special character is automatically appended to the end of a string enclosed in double quotes in C++?
questions.explanation: In C++, strings enclosed in double quotes are null-terminated, with the null character '\0' automatically appended to mark the end of the string.

questions.question: Which C++ standard library header must be included to use predefined mathematical functions like sqrt() and pow()?
questions.explanation: Mathematical functions such as sqrt(), pow(), ceil(), and floor() are declared in the <cmath> header library.

questions.question: What return type must be declared for a C++ function that does not return any value to its caller?
questions.explanation: A function that performs actions without returning a calculated result to the caller must specify void as its return type.

questions.question: Which operator in C++ is used to obtain the memory address of an existing variable?
questions.explanation: The ampersand (&) is the address-of operator, which produces the memory address of whichever variable it precedes.

questions.question: From which memory storage area is dynamic memory allocated when using the new operator in C++?
questions.explanation: Unlike normal local variables allocated on the runtime stack, dynamic objects created using new are allocated from the heap.

questions.question: Which stream class in C++ is specifically used for reading input from a disk file?
questions.explanation: The ifstream class stands for input-file stream and provides member functions for reading data from disk files.

questions.question: What is the default access mode when opening a disk file in C++?
questions.explanation: In C++, the default mode for file operations is text mode, which interprets files as standard ASCII characters.

questions.question: What are the four fundamental pillars of Object-Oriented Programming (OOP)?
questions.explanation: The four pillars of OOP defined in the material are abstraction, encapsulation, inheritance, and polymorphism.

questions.question: What is the default access specifier for members of a class in C++ if none is explicitly provided?
questions.explanation: In C++, members of a class are private by default, while members of a struct are public by default.

questions.question: What initial values are assigned to the elements of a global array declared outside all functions?
options: All elements are initialized to zero
All elements are initialized to negative one
All elements are set to null pointers
questions.explanation: Declaring a global array outside any function initializes all its elements to zero automatically.

questions.question: Which C-string manipulation function returns the length of a string without counting its null terminating character?
questions.explanation: strlen() calculates the number of valid characters in a string, excluding the final null character '\0'.

questions.question: What is the programming technique of breaking down an overall task into smaller subtasks to design an algorithm called?
options: Top-down design or divide and conquer
questions.explanation: Top-down design (or divide and conquer) breaks down a problem into a hierarchy of smaller subtasks.

questions.question: What happens to a local automatic variable when the function in which it is defined finishes execution?
options: It is preserved until the whole program ends
It is converted into a static global variable
It is moved into heap storage
questions.explanation: By default, local variables are automatic and are erased from the runtime stack once the function terminates.

questions.question: What does the dereference operator (*) produce when applied to a valid pointer variable?
options: The memory address of the pointer variable itself
The value stored at the memory location pointed to by the pointer
The total number of bytes occupied by the pointer
A boolean flag indicating if the pointer is null
questions.explanation: Dereferencing a pointer with * retrieves the actual data value stored at the memory location to which the pointer points.

questions.question: Which C++ operator is used to deallocate dynamic memory that was allocated for a single object?
questions.explanation: The delete operator is used in C++ to free memory allocated for a single object created with new.

questions.question: Which stream member function can be called to verify whether a file opening operation was unsuccessful?
questions.explanation: The fail() member function returns true if an operation such as opening a file could not be completed successfully.

questions.question: Which file access mode should be used to write data to the end of a file without overwriting existing contents?
questions.explanation: The ios::app mode opens a file in append mode, causing all write operations to be added to the end of the file.

questions.question: What is an identifiable runtime instance created from a class blueprint called in OOP?
questions.explanation: An object is an instance or replica of a class, holding state through data members and behavior through methods.

questions.question: Which operator is used to link a member function definition to its class name when defining it outside the class?
questions.explanation: The scope resolution operator (::) specifies the class scope when defining member functions outside the class header.

questions.question: What punctuation mark is required immediately after the closing brace of a structure definition in C++?
questions.explanation: In C++, all structure and class definitions must end with a closing curly brace followed by a semicolon.

questions.question: Which operator is used to access an individual member variable of a structure instance?
questions.explanation: The dot operator (.) is used with a structure variable name to access its members, with the syntax VarName.Member.

questions.question: Which components of a function declaration constitute its function signature in C++?
options: The function body and return statements
The function name and the types of its parameters
The parameter names and default values
The return type and function name
questions.explanation: A function signature in C++ consists of the function name and the types of its arguments; the return type is not part of the signature.

questions.question: What is a function that calls itself to solve a computational problem defined as?
questions.explanation: A function which calls itself during its execution is defined as a recursive function.

questions.question: Which type of pointer is designed to store the address of an object of any data type without being tied to a specific type?
questions.explanation: A void pointer (void*) is a generic pointer that can hold the memory address of any variable regardless of data type.

questions.question: What standardized keyword was introduced in modern C++ (C++11) to indicate a null pointer?
questions.explanation: In C++11 and later, nullptr is the dedicated literal used to represent a pointer that does not point to any valid memory location.

questions.question: Which member function must be called after completing file operations to release system resources?
questions.explanation: The close() member function disconnects the stream from the file, flushes remaining data, and releases system resources.

questions.question: Which stream member function reads a single character from an input stream without automatically skipping blanks?
questions.explanation: The get() member function reads the next single character of input, including spaces and newlines, without skipping whitespace.

questions.question: What is the OOP concept of wrapping data and the functions that manipulate that data into a single unit called?
questions.explanation: Encapsulation is the process of aggregating data and functions into a single unit (an object), enabling data hiding.

questions.question: Which special member function is automatically invoked when an object of a class is created and cannot return any value?
questions.explanation: A constructor is automatically executed when an object is declared to initialize member variables, and cannot have any return type.
